# T6.06: HEVC IDR at 720p, 1080p, 4K

First run with the T6.05 code (`encode1 -hevc W H 25`): 1080p, 1440p and 1366x768 fine (47.8 dB), but **720p 25.9 dB
and 4K 37.7 dB**. The failing sizes are the ones whose 16-aligned height leaves half a 32-row CTB at the bottom
(720 / 32 = 22.5, 2160 / 32 = 67.5); 1080 is coded as 1088 = 34 CTBs.

nullmoth's library at 1280x720 (`docs/traces/vttest-hevc-1280x720-2f.log`, `nm-hevc-1280x720-2f.h265`):
- **SPS 1280x736 with a conformance window** (bottom 8 units = 16 lines): the picture is coded in whole CTBs.
- Engine: reference/output surfaces `frame_height_minus1` 735, input surface 719 (the engine pads the source,
  `enable_source_image_padding`). Recon chroma at luma + 1280 x 736. `num_ctus` 920 = 40 x 23,
  `ceil_log2_pic_size_in_ctbs` 10.
- **`hist_buf_size` 30,720** (6,144 at 256x128): 768 bytes per CTB column. Our H.264-derived history buffer was 64 KB
  at 4K, where HEVC needs 92 KB: the second reason 4K broke.

Changes: `hevc_coded_width/height` round to 32 (the conformance window crops); `setup_hevc` gives the reference and
output surfaces the coded size (input keeps the display size); HEVC history buffer = 768 B x CTB columns.

| size | bits (QP 25) | luma | chroma |
|---|---|---|---|
| 256x128 | 7,600 | 48.23 dB | 49.60 dB |
| 640x360 | 45,536 | 48.04 dB | 49.89 dB |
| 1280x720 | 173,000 | 47.77 dB | 49.73 dB |
| 1360x760 | 196,512 | 47.79 dB | 49.70 dB |
| 1366x768 | 194,352 | 47.79 dB | 49.65 dB |
| 1920x1080 | 374,952 | 47.76 dB | 49.76 dB |
| 2560x1440 | 662,952 | 47.75 dB | 49.77 dB |
| 3840x2160 | 1,474,176 | 47.74 dB | 49.76 dB |

All decode with 0 errors; `hevchdrcheck` still passes. Still unknown: what the engine keeps in the extra 64 KB of each
reference slot (kept as nullmoth's); matters only for memory size.
